key_insight: Standard manipulation success metrics can hide object damage, so ManiPhysicsBench adds physics-based checks for preservation, not just task completion.
engineering_relevance: This matters for robotic handling of fragile or valuable parts because a policy should be judged by whether it manipulates safely without causing deformation or fracture.
method: ManiPhysicsZoo packages object assets with material properties, 3D meshes, and supporting references.
A solver estimates grasp-specific damage thresholds from geometry, material data, and observed grasp conditions, then compares them with contact forces.
ManiPhysicsBench evaluates VLA policies in LIBERO and SimplerEnv across three physics axes and three difficulty levels.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a large gap between task success and safe success across public VLA checkpoints, with gripper commands clustering near fully open/closed states.
watch_item: The retrained model improved safe success but reduced task success and showed limited generalization, so object-preserving behavior may not transfer robustly.
paper_title: ManiPhysicsBench: Physics-Based Assessment of Object Preservation in VLA Manipulation
